promptHead: Athlete goal: 5K (Corrowmore Harvest 5K) on Sun Nov 15 2026, 10 weeks out, target run the whole way.

new.headline: Keep three runs a week and don't run daily. Next week you run the same three mornings at a slower, easier pace, with one small step up on Saturday.

answers.question: I want to be ready for the 5K in November. Should I run every day next week to get there faster?
answers.answer:
No, running every day would slow you down rather than speed you up. Your legs get fitter on the days between runs, not during the runs themselves.

Your calves were tight the day after each run, which tells me they are still adapting to the load. Three runs a week with a rest or dog-walk day between them gives them time to catch up.

The faster route to running the whole 5K is to stay healthy for ten weeks and make your running segments a little longer each week. That is what the plan does inside the three runs you already do.

new.analysis:
Your first week was a good start. You ran three times, felt no pain, slept about 7 hours and reported normal stress. Heart rate stayed steady within each session, so your body is coping with the walk-run format.

The one thing to change is how hard the running segments feel. About a quarter of your heart-rate time was in zone 3, and you rated the sessions 6 to 7 out of 10, on a week with no hard work planned. That points to running segments that are too quick, not to a need for more walking. Slowing down is the fix.

The plan label says build, but for you that means longer running segments, not faster running. Threshold work and race-pace efforts have no place yet. Your aerobic fitness and the tendons in your lower legs need a few weeks of easy, repeatable running first.

Your sessions last week look like 1 min run and 1 min 30 walk on Monday and Wednesday, then 1 min 30 run and 1 min 30 walk on Saturday. Next week Monday and Wednesday move up to the Saturday pattern, and only Saturday asks for something new. Total running time rises from about 28 minutes to about 38, which is a fair step from a small base because the walks stay in.

Because your calves have been tight after runs, I have added one short bodyweight strength session on Friday. It sits two days after Wednesday's run, so your legs are fresh for Saturday. Keep it light and stop well before your legs feel tired.

A lighter week is due around Sep 14 – 20, the fourth week of running. After that the running segments keep lengthening every one to two weeks, and the walk breaks shrink. By the second half of the block you will be running for longer stretches, which is what the goal of running the whole way needs.
